newsitem.title: CANADA: Simmonds PowerTel plans wireless T.V..
newsitem.headline: Simmonds PowerTel plans wireless T.V..

text.p: PowerTel TV, wholly owned by Simmonds Capital Ltd, said on Wednesday it would seek regulatory approval to launch a wireless cable television service in the Toronto area.

PowerTel's newly-appointed president, Ted Boyle, told a news conference that the company plans to apply to the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission in the coming weeks with the hope of winning approval sometime next year.
"We believe the lack of competition (in the cable TV industry) will cause the CRTC to move quickly," he said.
Boyle was the former president of ExpressVu, a consortium that ran into technological and regulatory problems trying to get a direct to home satellite television service off the ground.

PowerTel said it hoped to offer a 100-channel digital service in the Toronto regional area that will include the new specialty channels recently licenced. It will employ so-called MMDS technology, or multichannel multipoint distribution system.

The system involves the transmission of satellite signals to a PowerTel base that are relayed using microwave signals to various towers, including the CN Tower in Toronto. Consumers pick up the signals from their home using a small flat antenna and a T.V. set top box.
Boyle said because the system does not require extensive infrastructure, it can be offered at a price lower than what has been charged by cable T.V. companies.
He would not say how much the start up development costs will be for the new service but maintained the company has the financial backing to launch it.
The CRTC has already issued one licence for wireless cable, to SkyCable Inc in Manitoba, which also uses MMDS technology.
PowerTel chairman Harry Dunstan said the service will also be used for speedy Internet connections, which would be used by computer users or connected to proposed Internet-ready television sets.
